item.title: Ticino, medical alarm: Teeth ask border crossers for limits
item.description: The president of the Order of Doctors of Ticino Franco Denti warns: Ticino has one doctor for every 900 inhabitants, at Como one for every 2,000. Ethical reflection is needed.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Ticino has one family doctor for every 900 inhabitants. - In the province of Como, the ratio is one doctor for every 2,000 people. - Franco Denti calls for an ethical reflection on the recruitment of health workers. - A strategy is needed to ensure attractiveness to the medical profession.
## Key facts - **What**: Alarm shortage of doctors and border nurses. - Where: Ticino and the province of Como. - Who: Franco Denti, president of the Order of Doctors of Ticino. - Doctors' ratio Ticino: 1 per 900 inhabitants. - Como doctors' report: 1 per 2,000 inhabitants. - Number of Ticino family doctors: Approximately 390.
The president of the Order of Doctors of Ticino, Franco Denti, raised an important issue regarding the maintenance of the regional health system and its relationship with the neighboring Italian territory. The situation in Ticino, characterized by the presence of about 390 family doctors for 351 thousand inhabitants, offers a framework of health coverage that appears significantly more solid than what has been observed across borders. In the province of Como, in fact, the number of active family doctors is less than 300 units for a population of about 598 thousand people, resulting in a significant disparity in the relationship between professionals and citizens. This gap, reconstructed through the comparison data between the two sides of the border, highlights how Switzerland represents an attractive destination for many health professionals trained in Italy.
### The Ethical Question The stability of the Ticino healthcare system is inextricably linked to the demographic challenges affecting the entire country. According to Franco Denti, generational turnover represents the next major test for local family medicine. Professionals from the baby boomer generation are nearing retirement age, and although there are no mandatory age limits for ending professional activity in Switzerland, turnover appears complex due to the smaller number of new medical graduates. The Canton is attempting to address this transition through targeted investments in academic training, particularly through the Faculty of Biomedical Sciences at the Università della Svizzera italiana. The master's degree dedicated to family medicine, which reports full classes, is a positive sign of how the attractiveness of the study path is an essential pillar for ensuring continuity of care.
### Strategies for professional attractiveness The concern expressed regarding the situation in Como reflects a fear also widespread in the Swiss context: the decline in medical vocations, which has intensified in the post-pandemic period. To prevent staff shortages from becoming a structural obstacle to economic development and the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) in terms of service efficiency, it is necessary to implement strategies that make the medical and nursing professions competitive. This does not only mean looking at salary conditions, but also at social status and the quality of daily work. A healthcare system that fails to train or retain professionals risks having to constantly resort to temporary solutions, increasing pressure on public accounts and on the [LAMal/KVG](nav:health) premiums paid by residents. The challenge for the Cantons, also closely monitored by federal offices, remains that of balancing dependence on the international labor market with the creation of a local talent pool capable of autonomously responding to the needs of an aging population. Ultimately, the stability of the system depends on the ability to transform training into a solid and lasting career opportunity, aligning the expectations of young doctors with the real needs of the territory, and preventing the reliance on foreign personnel from becoming the only possible response to the crisis of vocations.

For healthcare professionals working in Switzerland or intending to pursue a career in the Canton, understanding market dynamics is essential. The Swiss system, based on a solid salary structure that reflects the high cost of living and the high level of specialization required, necessitates careful planning, especially for those evaluating a life path between Italy and Switzerland. Doctors and nurses wishing to work in Swiss territory must deal with requirements for the recognition of academic qualifications and with cantonal regulations governing the practice of the profession. It is essential to constantly check open positions at healthcare companies and [hiring companies](nav:companies) for qualified personnel, monitoring professional growth opportunities offered by the hospital network and private practices. Career management in Switzerland also involves proper pension planning, which includes the second pillar [LPP/BVG](nav:pension) and potential tax optimization, aspects that every professional should delve into to protect their long-term position.
### Procedures and professional advice Those intending to settle or work in Ticino must follow precise procedures, ranging from obtaining residence or work permits (such as the G permit for cross-border commuters) to managing taxes and mandatory insurance. The complexity of the system requires a careful assessment of every administrative step, from tax returns to health insurance coverage, which must be taken out within strict deadlines upon arrival in the country. item.description: The medical equipment of a Swiss company stolen on Thursday morning was found in Rome. The equipment was recovered by the local police.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Stolen medical equipment recovered from a Swiss company - The theft took place on Thursday morning in Rome - The instruments were discovered in a green area in Rome - The Swiss company was able to complete the university presentation
## Key facts - **What**: Recovery of stolen medical equipment - When: Thursday, September 12, 2026 - Where: Rome, via Luigi Candoni - Who: Local police of Roma Capitale - Amount: High-value instrumentation
### Recovery of the equipment The high-value medical equipment stolen from a Swiss company's van was found abandoned in a green area located near the Roma nomad camp in via Luigi Candoni, in the Italian capital. The discovery was made thanks to the intervention of a patrol from the XI Marconi group of the local police of Roma Capitale, engaged in normal surveillance duty in the area. The local police officers immediately checked the serial numbers on the instruments, successfully establishing with certainty that the entire equipment belonged to a Swiss company. The equipment was found to have been stolen from a van that had been parked near a hotel located in the Aurelio district. The representatives of the Swiss company were in the city of Rome to take part in a practical demonstration scheduled at the headquarters of the Link Campus University. After noticing the theft, the employees of the Swiss company had filed a formal complaint with the competent authorities. The timely recovery of the medical equipment allowed the Swiss company to regularly complete the initiative that had been planned inside the Roman university. Currently, investigations are underway to reconstruct in detail the route taken by the stolen goods before the recovery and to identify those responsible for the theft. ### Ongoing investigations and the context of the theft
The competent authorities are continuing their investigations to clarify every aspect related to the theft suffered by the Swiss company during its trip to the capital. The episode directly involved the Swiss corporate representatives who arrived in Rome for an academic and demonstration commitment. The theft took place on Thursday morning when the company van, parked near a hotel in the Aurelio district, was targeted by criminals. The medical equipment being transported, characterized by a high economic and technical value, was stolen even before the official presentation scheduled inside the university campus could begin. The promptness of the investigations carried out by the local police officers of the XI Marconi group prevented the goods from being definitively lost or dispersed on the black market. Thanks to the precise verification of the serial numbers engraved on the devices, the local police quickly traced the Swiss company that owns the instruments. The goods were located in a green area near via Luigi Candoni, a peripheral area of the city near a nomad camp. This recovery avoided huge commercial and operational damages to the Swiss company, which was able to proceed without further delays with the practical demonstration planned at the Link Campus University. Law enforcement continues to work to identify the subjects responsible for the robbery and to understand the methods by which the van was broken into in the Aurelio district.

item.title: New US Tariffs and SECO Agreements for Swiss Companies
item.description: The United States introduces additional duties of up to 12.5% on Swiss goods. SECO monitors the impacts and evolution of production chains.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - US tariffs on Swiss goods starting July 24, 2026 - Maximum additional tariff of 12.5% - Free trade negotiations concluded on August 20, 2026 - SECO active in 32 countries with 900 employees
## Key facts - **What**: Introduction of additional US tariffs - When: July 24, 2026 - Where: United States / Switzerland - Who: SECO / US authorities - Amount: Up to 12.5%
On July 24, 2026, the United States formally adopted new restrictive measures in the form of additional tariffs, impacting imports originating from Switzerland. This decision stems from an investigation conducted by the US into trade in goods produced using forced labor, pursuant to Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974. For Swiss goods, the additional tariff rate is variable and can reach a maximum ceiling of 12.5%. It is understood that the calculation of final customs duties will still take into account MFN duties—namely those applied under the Most-Favored-Nation principle already in force in bilateral relations. On the diplomatic and economic relations front, it is noteworthy that, during a period of significant shifts in international flows, negotiations regarding the optimization of the free trade agreement officially concluded on August 20, 2026. The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, better known as SECO, represents the central federal body overseeing the evolution of such dossiers. The institution, which has over 900 employees distributed across three main offices in Switzerland and 50 posted across 32 countries, serves as the primary interlocutor for strategic economic policy issues. ### Organizational structure of the federal entity. SECO is divided into four distinct directorates, flanked by the Resources service area, with strategic governance entrusted to a steering committee. SECO management acts as a central discussion body for strategic issues, ensuring the operational continuity necessary to manage the challenges posed by the global trade context, including recent customs developments with the United States. The official website remains the point of reference for accessing essential information broken down by topic. The introduction of additional tariffs by the United States, based on the provisions of the Trade Act of 1974, requires Swiss export-oriented companies to thoroughly reflect on their procurement processes and production chains. The maximum threshold of 12.5% directly affects the final cost of products destined for the US market, requiring a review of profit margins and competitive positioning strategies. Prior to this measure, customs planning was based exclusively on MFN tariffs; now, the addition of a variable linked to the forced labor investigation changes the operational framework for Swiss economic operators. ### Analysis of impacts on production supply chains. For companies operating with complex supply chains, the impact is not limited to mere taxation, but requires rigorous mapping of production sources. Compliance with international regulations, closely monitored also by SECO, becomes an element of commercial survival. While previously attention was focused primarily on quality and price, today supply chain transparency plays a decisive role in avoiding the application of additional sanctions. It is possible to consult the cost of living [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) to better understand how macroeconomic dynamics influence domestic purchasing power, while for businesses, the management of customs costs becomes an integral part of financial planning. The comparison between the pre-July 24, 2026 situation and the current one highlights greater pressure on Swiss companies, called upon to demonstrate full compliance with the labor ethics requirements imposed by US authorities. The conclusion of negotiations on the optimization of the free trade agreement, which took place on August 20, 2026, could represent an attempt to mitigate the trade frictions that arose with the new measures. Companies intending to operate successfully must integrate these variables into their forecast budgets, constantly monitoring communications from SECO and foreign customs authorities to promptly adapt to any regulatory changes.

It is essential to maintain an up-to-date archive of origin certifications and production processes, ready to be presented in the event of thorough customs audits. item.title: Salt: cyber attack and theft of mobile customer data
item.description: The Salt telephone operator victim of a cyber-attack. Personal data of some mobile customers in Switzerland was stolen. The Federal Appointee has been notified.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Salt operator is the victim of a cyber attack - Subtracted personal data of some mobile customers - The Federal Data Protection Officer has been notified - No password or bank details compromised
## Key facts - **What**: Cyberattack and theft of personal data - When: Friday afternoon - Where: Switzerland - Who: Salt Telephone Operator
The telephone operator salt was the victim of a cyber attack that led to the theft of personal data of some mobile phone customers in Switzerland. The company confirmed the incident by informing the affected customers during the afternoon of Friday. Information that has been stolen from the systems includes users' first and last names, dates of birth, postal addresses, email addresses and mobile phone numbers associated with mobile phone users.
### Details on stolen information and notification
At the moment, the authorities and the company have not yet specified precisely how many people were affected by this cyber attack in Switzerland, nor has the exact time or day of the intrusion into Salt's computer systems been disclosed. However, the telephone operator wanted to clarify in a timely manner that the most sensitive customer data, such as access passwords, bank information or personal credentials, are not compromised in any way. Although the company has ruled out the compromise of particularly critical data such as banking credentials or passwords, the incident raises important questions regarding security management and the protection of personal information in the Swiss telecommunications market. When events of this nature occur, the practical implications for resident citizens mainly concern the risk of exposure to telephone fraud attempts, targeted phishing campaigns, or deceptive communications that exploit the stolen information to appear more reliable. The presence of personal and contact data such as addresses and mobile numbers actually offers malicious actors a privileged channel to attempt scams against the affected users. ### Analysis of reporting procedures and the role of federal authorities A relevant aspect of the affair concerns the institutional management of the personal data breach. Salt also proceeded to notify the incident to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, who confirmed having received the report directly from the telephone company. According to what was specified by Salt, this communication to the authorities took place on a voluntary basis. This is a specific procedure that is adopted when the company believes that the actual risks to the fundamental rights and personality of the individuals involved are not particularly high. This scenario distinguishes the episode from other situations in which notification to the competent authorities is strictly mandatory by law based on the severity of the compromise of corporate and personal data.

In particular, it is advisable to always verify the authenticity of the messages received, avoiding clicking on unknown links or providing additional personal information even if the senders seem to refer to correct personal data previously stolen during the computer intrusion into the telephone company's systems.

item.title: Crans-Montana: fired employee for building fakes
item.description: The Municipality of Crans-Montana has dismissed a collaborator of the Technical Office for the falsification of documents relating to a terrace.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The Municipality of Crans-Montana has dismissed an employee of the Technical Office. - The measure follows the falsification of documents for a terrace. - The employee was already involved in the investigation of the Constellation tragedy.
## Key facts - **What**: Immediate dismissal for falsification of building documents. - When: 11 September 2026. - Where: Municipality of Crans-Montana. - Who: Employee of the Municipal Technical Office. - Motivation: Identity theft and compromise of the relationship of trust.
On 11 September 2026, the Municipality of Crans-Montana formalised the dismissal with immediate effect of a collaborator in force at its Technical Office. The decision, officially communicated by the municipal councillor François Berclaz, comes at the end of a rapid internal investigation, initiated following the discovery of serious administrative irregularities related to the management of a construction application. Specifically, the investigation established the falsification of an official document relating to the terrace of the Constellation premises. The abuse involved the usurpation of the identity of a civil engineer, whose name was entered into the construction practice without his knowledge. The professional, heard by law enforcement, confirmed that he had never been involved in the project, learning of what happened only fortuitously in January through a journalistic report.
### The dynamics of the facts According to The dismissal of a public official for falsifying building documents represents a particularly serious case that goes beyond simple personnel management, touching upon the control mechanisms that Swiss municipalities exercise over construction permits. The practice of verifying the validity of professional qualifications, as required for authors of construction projects, is a fundamental pillar of built environment safety. When this filter is bypassed through identity theft, the entire cantonal and municipal supervisory system suffers a crack. It is worth remembering that in Switzerland, the procedure for building permits follows strict protocols defined by the individual cantons, but based on common principles of professional responsibility. The responsibility of the project author is not merely formal, but implies the assumption of legal and technical burdens in the event of defects or accidents.
### Legal and Criminal Implications The dismissed employee is no stranger to judicial chronicles: he is indeed among the 17 people indicted for manslaughter, involuntary arson, and grievous bodily harm through negligence in relation to the Constellation tragedy, which occurred in December 2025. The fire caused 41 deaths and over 100 injuries, a tragedy that deeply shook public opinion. Already in May 2026, during an interrogation, the official had admitted to not having verified the compliance of a smoking room inaugurated in the basement in 2017, which had never been subjected to public inquiry. This precedent, combined with the recent document falsification, outlines a picture of reiterated negligence within the offices responsible for safety. For citizens and industry operators, this case underlines the importance of carefully monitoring building practices affecting their properties or commercial activities. It is possible to consult local regulations through municipal portals or contact cantonal technical offices to verify the progress of procedures. Anyone managing renovations or structural modifications must ensure that every signature on official documents is authentic and attributable to regularly licensed professionals, avoiding shortcuts that can expose them to extremely serious criminal and civil liabilities. The standard procedure allows for the consultation of publication files at the municipal technical offices during the public exhibition period of construction applications. If the improper use of one's name or a discrepancy between the filed project and reality is detected, a formal report must be submitted to the competent cantonal supervisory authority. It is never advisable to accept informal solutions or verbal agreements with officials suggesting circumventing current regulations, as the legal consequences, as demonstrated by the ongoing criminal investigation, can be severe and involve clients as well as technicians.

item.title: F-35A: Fixed Price Doubts and Parliamentary Reactions
item.description: The report on the lack of a fixed price for the F-35A shocks Parliament. Green toward the ICC, while the center-right brakes.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Critical report on the absence of a fixed price for the F-35A jets. - The center-right in Parliament opposes a parliamentary commission of inquiry. - Viola Amherd will not issue further statements on the dossier. - The Greens are evaluating a motion for a parliamentary commission of inquiry in the autumn session.
## Key facts - **What**: Lack of a fixed price for the purchase of F-35A fighter jets. - Where: Bern, Swiss Parliament. - Who: Control Committee of the National Council, Viola Amherd, The Greens. - Amount: 400 million francs requested as a supplementary credit. - Status: No immediate consequences, political debate ongoing.
The report drawn up by the Control Committee of the National Council regarding the acquisition of the F-35A fighter jets has sparked strong controversy in Bern, revealing the absence of a contractual fixed price. This discovery had the effect of a political bombshell, although the regulatory and procedural framework will not undergo changes in the immediate future. The former Defense Minister, Viola Amherd, made it known through Keystone-ATS that she had already expressed her position on the matter, stating that she did not wish to make further comments on the charges contained in the document. The Swiss political class appears deeply divided: while the center-right, which holds the majority in Parliament, has already expressed itself negatively on the possibility of establishing a parliamentary commission of inquiry (CPI), the Greens are pushing decisively for this solution to shed light on what happened. ### Party reactions and parliamentary debate. Despite the divergence of views on the need for a formal investigation, the contents of the report have caused transversal consternation. National Councilor Clarence Chollet, a member of the Greens, defined the impact on Switzerland's image as catastrophic. In parallel, the UDC group leader, Thomas Aeschi, raised doubts about the management of the dossier, asking to clarify who was responsible for supervision and whether the law firm involved operated in total autonomy or under control. The FDP, for its part, insists on the need to restore a relationship of trust between the executive and the Federal Chambers, underlining that parliamentarians must be able to access clear and precise information during acquisition processes of such magnitude. The climate of uncertainty remains high, waiting to see how parliamentary discussions will evolve in the coming sessions. The analysis of the potential legal consequences surrounding the F-35A fighter jet affair offers food for thought regarding administrative and political accountability within the Swiss context. Andreas Stöckli, professor of constitutional and administrative law at the University of Fribourg, explained that assessing the liability of federal administration employees is extremely complex. The requirements for claiming financial liability are, by law, very strict: it would be necessary to prove the existence of illicit conduct committed with intent or through gross negligence. In the absence of such prerequisites, it is unlikely that administrative personnel or the law firms involved in the acquisition will face legal proceedings. ### Immunity and the role of politics. Regarding the issue of criminal liability, Vincent Martenet, professor of constitutional law at the University of Lausanne, also weighed in. He recalled that members of the Federal Council enjoy absolute immunity concerning statements made officially before the Federal Chambers. Therefore, the judicial path appears almost impracticable, leaving the political route as the only option, namely the establishment of a parliamentary commission of inquiry. However, the path to achieving such a commission remains uphill. Pierre-Alain Fridez, former Socialist National Councilor, expressed in an interview with the newspaper '24 heures' his fear that the parliamentary majority will limit itself to interpreting the event as a misreading of the contracts, avoiding a deeper investigation into political responsibilities. The Socialist Party has therefore requested that the Federal Council verify the possible presence of false statements that could constitute criminal offenses. This position is also reflected in budget management: the left seems inclined to deny its support for the request for a supplementary credit of nearly 400 million francs intended for the purchase of the American aircraft. The situation remains in a stalemate, with the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) continuing to be a central theme in the debate on national public spending.

item.title: Tag der Wirtschaft: Guy Parmelin's speech in Lucerne
item.description: Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin speaks at the Tag der Wirtschaft in Lucerne, taking stock of Switzerland's economic resilience and free trade agreements.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin's speech at the Tag der Wirtschaft - Review of the economic situation and Swiss resilience - Focus on free trade agreements and international relations
## Key facts - **What**: Official speech at the Swiss Economy Day - When: September 11, 2026 - Where: Lucerne - Who: Guy Parmelin, Head of the EAER - Amount: Second-quarter GDP growth at its highest level since 2021
On September 11, 2026, in Lucerne, the Head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research, Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin, delivered his speech at the Tag der Wirtschaft, the traditional gathering of the Swiss business community. The event also marked Christoph Mäder's farewell from the presidency of economiesuisse, a significant institutional transition for the national economic fabric. The speech opened by outlining the global economic framework characterized by geopolitical tensions, trade conflicts, and uncertainties in export markets, compounded by demographic transition and rapid technological evolution.
### Resilience and macroeconomic indicators
Despite international difficulties, Parmelin emphasized how Switzerland maintains remarkable economic and financial stability. Unemployment remains at relatively low levels, inflation is under control, and public finances show solid foundations. During the second quarter, gross domestic product recorded an acceleration in growth not seen since the third quarter of 2021. According to the federal executive, this result is not accidental but is the fruit of an economic model based for decades on openness, competition, individual responsibility, and favorable institutional framework conditions. The business fabric, consisting of small and medium-sized enterprises, multinationals, start-ups, and family-run businesses, represents the engine of this stability, operating daily on global markets.
### The role of the State and competitiveness
In his speech, the representative of the Federal Council reiterated the limits of public intervention in the market economy. The State has the task of guaranteeing legal certainty, investing in key sectors of education and research, and opening foreign markets through economic diplomacy. However, Parmelin recalled that innovation does not originate inside the Federal Palace, jobs do not stem from simple government decisions, and collective well-being cannot be imposed by decree. To delve deeper into the employment framework and opportunities in the labor market, it is possible to consult the section dedicated to [hiring companies](nav:companies). Given the limitations of the Swiss domestic market, the absence of relevant raw materials, and the presence of high production costs, national prosperity remains closely linked to the ability to maintain high standards of innovation, quality, and export. ### The opening strategy and trade treaties
The prosperity of the nation depends crucially on access to international markets, a vital element for a strongly export-oriented economy. ## In brief - Growth of transalpine freight traffic by 3.1% in the first half of 2026 - Railway market share at 68%, down by 0.9 percentage points - Increase in road transport and truck journeys reaching 511,000 - Single wagonload freight traffic recorded an 8% decline
## Key facts - **What**: Federal Office of Transport semi-annual reports on freight traffic - When: First half of 2026 - Where: Switzerland, transalpine and north-south axis - Who: Federal Office of Transport and Federal Council - Amount: 12 million franc loss for SBB Cargo in single wagonload freight
In the first half of 2026, Swiss railways transported a higher volume of goods through the Alps compared to the corresponding period of the previous year. According to reports published in Bern by the Federal Office of Transport, the growth recorded by the railway sector stands at 3.1 percent. Despite this growth, the increase in road transport proved to be significantly higher, leading to a slight contraction in the railway's market share in transalpine freight traffic, which now stands at 68 percent.
Both rail and road benefited from a favorable economic environment and an expanding overall market during the first six months of the year. However, truck journeys grew by approximately 7 percent, reaching 511,000. Based on this trend, projections indicate that by the end of 2026 the annual number of trips made by trucks will once again exceed one million, a milestone that has not been recorded for a long time in the heavy road transport sector across Swiss territory.
### Critical issues on the north-south axis
An element of severe pressure for rail freight traffic remains the numerous construction sites along the north-south axis, the negative impact of which is felt particularly in Germany. The complex infrastructural situation limits the fluidity of rail connections, and competent authorities estimate that an effective improvement will not materialize before around 2030. To counteract these difficulties and support the sector, the Federal Council has included additional financial resources within the current revision of the freight transport law, specifically aimed at boosting rail freight traffic through the Alps.
At the same time, single wagonload freight transport, which represents an essential pillar for domestic, import, and export logistics nationwide, is going through a phase of operational contraction. During the first six months of 2026, the number of loaded wagons used in this mode showed an 8 percent decrease compared to data recorded in the same period of the previous year, while costs per single wagon stabilized. The analysis of the half-yearly data published by the Federal Office of Transport highlights divergent dynamics between the different modes of freight transport in Switzerland, reflecting the reactivity of the market in the face of cyclical and structural factors. On the one hand, the rubber sector benefits from greater immediate operational flexibility, which has allowed it to absorb demand growth with an increase in truck runs of 7 percent. On the other hand, the railway meets the structural limits deriving from international shipyards and the congestion of the foreign network, in particular German, which penalize the competitiveness of north-south transits along the Alpine routes.
The Confederation actively intervenes to support the railway sector through targeted subsidies, as in the case of isolated wagon traffic, for which constant semi-annual monitoring has been introduced. Despite the public indemnities paid in the reference period, SBB Cargo closed the first half of 2026 with a negative economic result in the sector of isolated complete wagon transport, registering a loss of 12 million francs compared to 40 million francs of financial support received. ## Key facts - * * What * *: Ultra Broadband Bill - When: ITER started in 2016, updated in 2023 and 2024 - Where: Swiss Confederation and outlying regions - Who: Federal Council and Federal Chambers - Amount: CHF 365 million
The Federal Council has decided to implement with a specific proposal for a law the cantonal initiative originally presented by the national socialist councilor Bruno Storni, entitled 'Guaranteeing a widespread offer of ultra-broadband services throughout the national territory'. The announcement was made by Bruno Storni himself through a post on the Facebook social platform, highlighting the arrival of positive news directly from Bern for digital connectivity in Switzerland. The total appropriation budgeted by the federal government amounts to 365 million francs, a figure that will be gradually spread and disbursed over eight years to support the less densely populated areas of the country.
### Origins of the cantonal initiative
The measure has its roots in a cantonal initiative formalized in Ticino in 2015, which made an explicit request for widespread coverage of ultra-broadband services extended to the entire Swiss national territory. The technological and regulatory evolution linked to this digitisation plan has seen fundamental milestones in recent years. Already in 2023, the federal authorities adopted the so-called 'Gigabit Strategy', a programmatic approach aimed at guaranteeing a connection speed of at least 1 Gbit/s in download through the fixed network connections available in the territory. At the same time, following the long parliamentary process, the Confederation has decided to increase the level of mandatory universal service to 80 Mbps from 2024. This technical threshold currently places the Swiss network among the highest levels internationally in terms of the provision of basic telecommunications infrastructure.
### The current legislative process
The transformation of the cantonal initiative into an organic law text represents the next crucial institutional step. The regulatory package prepared by the Federal Council is now submitted to the formal examination of the Federal Chambers, which will have to debate, evaluate and possibly approve the operational and financial details of the measure before its definitive entry into force in the Swiss regulatory system.

item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Sostegno mensile per figli e giovani in formazione nel Canton Giura - Gestione tramite cassa di compensazione competente - Procedura di domanda basata su condizioni di diritto specifiche - Importi differenziati tra assegni familiari e di formazione
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Assegni familiari e di formazione - Dove: Canton Giura - Chi: Genitori/tutori con figli a carico - Importo: Definito dalle scale cantonali (non ancora specificato nel dettaglio) - Ente: Cassa di compensazione competente
Il sistema di previdenza sociale svizzera prevede, nel Canton Giura, l'erogazione di assegni familiari volti a sostenere i costi legati alla crescita e all'istruzione dei figli. Questi contributi rappresentano un pilastro fondamentale per l'economia domestica dei residenti, integrando il reddito salariale attraverso trasferimenti diretti gestiti dalle casse di compensazione. L'accesso a tali prestazioni non è automatico, ma richiede la verifica di precise condizioni di diritto legate alla residenza, al legame di parentela e all'età dei beneficiari.
### Tipologie di assegni previsti Nel Canton Giura si distinguono principalmente due categorie di prestazioni. Gli assegni familiari sono destinati ai figli fino al raggiungimento di una determinata soglia d'età, mentre gli assegni di formazione intervengono quando il giovane prosegue gli studi o intraprende un apprendistato, estendendo il periodo di sostegno finanziario. Questa distinzione assicura che il supporto economico sia allineato alle effettive necessità della famiglia, che variano significativamente tra l'infanzia e l'adolescenza.
L'erogazione di questi importi è strettamente legata alla normativa cantonale, che definisce le soglie di accesso e le modalità di calcolo. Poiché ogni Cantone gestisce autonomamente le proprie scale di importi, è essenziale fare riferimento agli aggiornamenti della cassa di compensazione di riferimento per conoscere le cifre esatte applicate nell'anno in corso. La gestione amministrativa segue i principi della previdenza sociale svizzera, coordinandosi con le istituzioni federali come l'UFAS/BSV per quanto riguarda i quadri normativi generali della previdenza. ## Analisi delle condizioni di diritto L'ottenimento degli assegni familiari nel Canton Giura dipende dal soddisfacimento di criteri rigorosi. Il richiedente deve dimostrare il legame di parentela o di tutela legale nei confronti del figlio. Un aspetto cruciale riguarda la residenza e l'attività lavorativa: i diritti agli assegni sono generalmente legati all'essere soggetti all'obbligo contributivo AVS/AHV nel territorio svizzero o, in specifici casi coordinati, in base agli accordi internazionali per chi risiede all'estero ma lavora in Svizzera.
### Scenari di formazione e istruzione Un'implicazione pratica rilevante riguarda il passaggio dagli assegni familiari a quelli di formazione. In uno scenario ipotetico, un giovane che completa l'obbligo scolastico e inizia un percorso di formazione professionale continua a generare un diritto al sostegno finanziario per i genitori. Questo meccanismo evita che l'uscita dal sistema scolastico primario causi un'improvvisa interruzione del supporto economico, facilitando l'inserimento nel mercato del lavoro attraverso l'apprendistato.
Il costo della vita in Svizzera, che incide pesantemente su affitti e assicurazioni malattia LAMal/KVG, rende questi assegni un elemento di stabilità. Sebbene l'importo non copra l'intera spesa di mantenimento, esso contribuisce a mitigare l'impatto finanziario delle spese scolastiche e dei materiali didattici. È utile confrontare questi importi con le deduzioni fiscali disponibili nella dichiarazione delle imposte tax-return, poiché gli assegni familiari possono influenzare il calcolo del reddito imponibile a seconda delle leggi cantonali e comunali vigenti nel Giura.
L'interazione tra previdenza e fiscalità è un punto chiave: mentre l'assegno è un beneficio previdenziale, la sua gestione richiede una documentazione accurata che deve essere presentata annualmente o al variare delle condizioni familiari. La precisione nella dichiarazione dei dati evita rimborsi retroattivi o sanzioni per indebiti percepiti, garantendo un flusso di cassa costante per il nucleo familiare.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Procedura di domanda e iter amministrativo Per richiedere gli assegni familiari nel Canton Giura, il primo passo consiste nell'identificare la cassa di compensazione competente. Solitamente, per i lavoratori dipendenti, la domanda viene inoltrata tramite il datore di lavoro, che funge da intermediario tra il dipendente e l'ente previdenziale. Per i lavoratori indipendenti, la domanda va presentata direttamente alla cassa di compensazione a cui sono affiliati per i contributi AVS/AHV.
### Documentazione necessaria e step operativi La procedura richiede la compilazione di un modulo ufficiale di domanda. I documenti solitamente richiesti includono: - Certificato di nascita del figlio o prova del legame di parentela - Attestati di studio o contratto di apprendistato per gli assegni di formazione - Documenti d'identità validi - Eventuali certificati di residenza se richiesti dall'ente
Una volta presentata la domanda, la cassa di compensazione verifica i requisiti di diritto. In caso di esito positivo, l'importo viene versato mensilmente. È fondamentale segnalare tempestivamente qualsiasi cambiamento nella situazione familiare (come la nascita di un nuovo figlio o il termine degli studi di un giovane) per aggiornare l'importo dell'assegno.
Per chi desidera pianificare il budget familiare includendo queste entrate, è consigliabile utilizzare strumenti di calcolo per stimare il reddito netto mensile. Considerare l'impatto di questi assegni insieme agli altri costi fissi, come i premi della cassa malati o i contributi LPP/BVG, permette una gestione finanziaria più accurata. Per una stima completa delle entrate mensili, è possibile utilizzare il nostro [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator), che aiuta a visualizzare l'impatto delle detrazioni e dei benefici sul salario netto.
⚠️ Ricordate che le scadenze per l'invio della domanda e i termini di prescrizione per le richieste retroattive sono definiti dalla legge cantonale e federale; pertanto, l'invio tempestivo della documentazione è l'unico modo per garantire la ricezione dei fondi a partire dalla data di maturazione del diritto.

item.description: Deductibles, alternative models and cantonal subsidy requirements: a practical guide to LAMal awards in the Canton of Vaud.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - LAMal obbligatoria per tutti i residenti, premi pro capite - Franchigie adulti da 300 a 2500 franchi - Riduzione premi è un sussidio cantonale, non automatico - Domanda va inoltrata all'ente cantonale competente
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Assicurazione malattia obbligatoria (LAMal) nel Canton Vaud - Quando: Da stipulare entro 3 mesi dall'arrivo in Svizzera - Dove: Cantone di Vaud, con premi regionali - Chi: Tutti i residenti, con riduzione premi per redditi bassi - Importo: Franchigie da CHF 300 a CHF 2500 per adulti
Il Cantone di Vaud, come tutti i cantoni svizzeri, applica la legge federale sull'assicurazione malattia (LAMal). Ogni residente deve stipulare una copertura di base entro tre mesi dall'arrivo. Il premio è individuale e varia per cantone e regione, non è una tassa né un contributo salariale, ma un costo diretto a carico dell'assicurato.
La scelta della franchigia è uno dei fattori che incide maggiormente sul premio. Per gli adulti, le opzioni vanno da 300 a 2500 franchi all'anno. Chi sceglie una franchigia più alta paga premi mensili più bassi, ma in caso di cure deve coprire personalmente una quota maggiore di spese. I modelli alternativi (come il medico di famiglia o il teleconsulto) permettono di ridurre ulteriormente il costo del premio, vincolando l'assicurato a determinate modalità di accesso alle cure.
### Il sistema a tre livelli La sanità svizzera si basa su una ripartizione chiara di competenze: la Confederazione definisce il quadro legale, i cantoni gestiscono l'assicurazione malattia e la riduzione dei premi, mentre i comuni non hanno un ruolo diretto in questo ambito. L'Ufficio federale della sanità pubblica (UFSP) supervisiona il sistema, ma non fissa i premi, che sono determinati dalle casse malati sulla base dei costi sanitari regionali.
Per chi ha un reddito modesto, esiste la riduzione dei premi: un sussidio cantonale che abbassa l'importo mensile da pagare. I requisiti dipendono dal reddito e dalla sostanza, e la domanda va presentata all'ente cantonale competente. Nel Canton Vaud, come altrove, la riduzione non è automatica: va richiesta ogni anno e viene calcolata sulla base della situazione fiscale dell'assicurato. ## Analisi pratica: come scegliere e risparmiare La scelta della franchigia è una decisione che va valutata con attenzione. Un adulto sano che non prevede spese mediche elevate può optare per una franchigia di 2500 franchi, riducendo il premio mensile in modo significativo. Al contrario, chi ha bisogno di cure regolari (fisioterapia, farmaci cronici, visite specialistiche) potrebbe trovarsi a spendere di più se sceglie una franchigia alta, perché deve coprire personalmente le prime spese fino al raggiungimento dell'importo.
I modelli alternativi sono un'altra leva per contenere i costi. Il modello del medico di famiglia, ad esempio, richiede di rivolgersi sempre al proprio medico di base, che poi indirizza agli specialisti. Il modello teleconsulto prevede di contattare prima un centro telefonico. Questi modelli offrono premi ridotti, ma impongono un percorso di cura più rigido. Nel Canton Vaud, come nel resto della Svizzera, le casse malati pubblicano i premi per ciascun modello e ciascuna franchigia, permettendo un confronto diretto.
### Prima e dopo: cosa cambia con la riduzione premi La riduzione dei premi è un meccanismo che esiste da decenni, ma i criteri di eleggibilità vengono aggiornati periodicamente. Chi ha diritto al sussidio lo riceve sotto forma di sconto diretto sul premio mensile, oppure come rimborso annuale, a seconda delle modalità del cantone. Senza la domanda, il sussidio non viene concesso: è responsabilità dell'assicurato presentare la richiesta entro i termini stabiliti.
Per chi arriva in Svizzera per lavoro, la questione è particolarmente rilevante. Il salario lordo non tiene conto dei premi, che vanno pagati separatamente. In un cantone con premi medi come Vaud, il costo mensile può incidere in modo significativo sul bilancio familiare. Per questo, conviene verificare subito se si ha diritto alla riduzione, presentando la domanda all'ufficio cantonale competente, solitamente collegato al servizio delle contribuzioni.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to get the reduction: step-by-step procedure 1. **Check requirements**: Premium reduction depends on taxable income and substance. Check the Canton of Vaud's website for updated income limits. 2. Prepare the documentation: You will need the last tax return, if already filed, or an income estimate if you have just arrived. 3. Submit the application: The application is submitted to the cantonal body in charge, usually via an online or paper form. The expiry is typically within a certain period from the beginning of the insurance year. 4. Wait for the decision: The office evaluates your situation and communicates the amount of the subsidy, which will be deducted from the monthly premiums. 5. Renew every year: The reduction is not automatic: it must be requested again every year, based on the updated tax situation.
If you have any doubts about the deductible or the most suitable model, use our [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator) to understand how much the premium affects your net income. To compare health insurance offers, you can use the [comparatore LAMal](nav:health). And if you're considering moving to another canton, keep in mind that the premiums vary: the [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) in Switzerland also depends on this factor.
Do not wait: the premium reduction is a right that must be exercised. A late application may result in the loss of the grant for the current year.

item.title: Naturalization in St. Gallen: requirements and procedure
item.description: Find out about the requirements for years, integration tests, language and fees for ordinary naturalisation in the canton of St. Gallen.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ordinary naturalization in St. Gallen requires integration and language tests - There is a naturalization fee to be paid - The procedure can take several months, depending on the municipality
## Key Facts - **What**: years requirements, integration test, language, fees - Where: Canton of St. Gallen, municipality of residence - Who: applicant with C permit - Amount: naturalization fee (not yet specified)
The Canton of St. Gallen has published guidelines for ordinary naturalization. The procedure is divided into several stages: the applicant must prove that he or she has lived for a period determined by both the canton and the municipality of residence, pass an integration test and a language test, and pay the required fees. The necessary residence permit is the C permit, which is usually obtained after ten years of residence (with a double count for the years between the 8th and 18th).
The cantonal and municipal authorities work together to check the residence time requirements: the canton sets a minimum number of years, while the municipality can request an additional period. Only after meeting these criteria can the applicant access the integration test, which assesses knowledge of Swiss culture, institutions and norms. At the same time, it is mandatory to pass the language test, which varies depending on the level required by the municipality.
Once the applicant has passed the tests, he or she must pay the naturalization fee. The amount varies depending on the canton and municipality, but it is a fixed item in the procedure. After payment, the application is reviewed by the municipality, which forwards the file to the canton. The total time, from the submission of the application to the granting of citizenship, can extend to several months, depending on how quickly the municipality completes the documentary verification.
> "The new cantonal legislation establishes that citizenship is not granted if the integration requirements are not fully met".
### National tax environment The Swiss tax system has three levels of taxation – federal, cantonal and municipal – and each canton applies its own multiplier. The naturalisation tax is also part of the cantonal component, so it is advisable to check the exact amount with the tax office in your municipality. For more details on the tax return, please consult the tax-return service. ## Practical analysis The naturalization process in St. Gallen has concrete implications for those who live and work in Switzerland. First of all, the requirement of years of residence imposes long-term planning: those who have just obtained a C permit must take into account that the counting of years begins from the moment the permit is issued and that, for individuals between 8 and 18 years of age, the years count double. This can reduce the time it takes to reach the cantonal threshold, but at the same time requires a careful verification of the periods recognized by the municipality.
The integration test, although not specified in detail, is a common element in all cantons. Its assessment includes knowledge of Swiss democratic institutions, the values of neutrality and the system of direct democracy. Preparation may require specific courses offered by cantonal bodies or private schools. At the same time, the language test is essential: the canton of St. Gallen requires mastery of German, with a level that varies depending on the municipality. Those coming from a French-speaking or Italian-speaking area will have to invest time in language courses to meet this requirement.
From an economic point of view, the naturalization fee represents an additional cost. Although the amount is not indicated, it is an expense to be included in the family budget, especially for those who already have commitments related to direct federal taxes, VAT and AHV/AHV contributions. In addition, the duration of the procedure – several months – means that applicants will have to maintain full KVG insurance coverage throughout the process, since citizenship does not alter insurance status.
A comparison with other cantons shows that St. Gallen follows the national logic but may differ in terms of the number of years required by the municipality and the amount of the tax. If you have already started the procedure in another canton, you should check whether the periods of residence already accrued are recognized by St. Gallen, otherwise you may have to supplement additional years. This is crucial for professionals who change their domicile for business reasons.
### Impact on the labour market Holding Swiss citizenship can facilitate access to public jobs and certain categories of employment that require citizenship. In addition, citizenship eliminates the need to periodically renew one's residence permit, reducing administrative uncertainty for employees and employers. For those interested in assessing the impact on their paycheck, the [payslip](nav:payslip) calculator can provide an estimate of AHV/AHV, BVG and other deductions after obtaining citizenship.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Step-by-step action 1. **Check your residence permit**: make sure you have a C permit, a fundamental requirement for ordinary naturalization. 2. Calculate the years of residence: count the years of presence in Switzerland since the C permit was issued; remember that the years between 8 and 18 count double. If the total does not yet reach the cantonal minimum, continue to reside regularly. 3. Gather documentation: integration certificates, language certificate (German), extracts from the population register, proof of payment of fees, and any employment certificates. All documents must be translated into German if necessary and notarized. 4. Submit the application to the municipality: send the complete dossier to the competent municipal office. The municipality will carry out an initial check and may request additions. 5. Take the tests: Take the integration test and the language test organized by the canton or municipality. Prepare yourself with specific courses or teaching materials provided by the authorities. 6. Pay the naturalisation fee: pay the amount required by the canton; keep the receipt for the next step. 7. Wait for the cantonal decision: the canton examines the file, verifies the results of the tests and the regularity of the payments. The response time varies, but it is normal to wait several months. 8. Final registration: Once citizenship has been granted, register your new status with the tax office and update your KVG insurance.
Throughout the process, it is advisable to keep an eye on tax and contribution deadlines. To assess the impact of citizenship on the overall tax burden, use our calculator dedicated to taxes and social contributions.
⚠️ Please note: if the municipality requests an additional period of residence, the count of years must also include this time frame; otherwise, the application will be rejected.
💡 Practical tip: Organize a digital checklist with all required documents and payment deadlines; this reduces the risk of omissions and speeds up the process.
### Next steps Once you have citizenship, you will be able to access all political rights (federal, cantonal, and municipal vote) and greater employment stability. To learn more about the tax and social security implications, check out our [pension](nav:pension) and cost-of-living to assess your new household budget.

## In a nutshell - Identical federal lease right in all cantons (CO art. 253 et seq.) - Maximum security deposit of 3 months on a restricted account in the name of the tenant - Lessor's cancellation valid only on official cantonal form - Dispute initial fee within 30 days to the conciliation authority
## Key facts - **What**: Federal Rules on Deposit, Cancellation and Rent Dispute - When: Valid without expiry, applicable to each new contract - Where: Canton of St. Gallen and all of Switzerland - Who: Cantonal landlords, tenants, conciliation authorities - Amount: Deposit max 3 rents; cancellation terms 1/2/3 months for seniority
The right to rent in Switzerland is governed at the federal level by the Code of Obligations (CO art. 253 et seq.) and applies identically in the Canton of St. Gallen as in the rest of the country. This means that the rules on security deposit, form of cancellation and contestation of the initial fee do not vary from one canton to another.
### Security deposit and escrow account The law sets a maximum limit: the deposit cannot exceed three months' rent (including ancillary charges). The sum must be paid into a restricted account in the tenant's name with a Swiss bank; the landlord cannot dispose of it freely. ## In brief - Ticino is not aging thanks to immigration - More 25-35 year-olds arrive than leave - The intercantonal balance towards other Cantons is negative - Those who study north of the Alps return in 55% of cases

Despite Ticino losing its young people, the population is not aging thanks to the fundamental contribution of immigration. This is revealed by data from a recent analysis conducted by the Cantonal Office of Statistics (USTAT) and explored in an interview with Francesco Giudici, head of the USTAT Society Sector. The survey focuses on the 25 to 35 age group, outlining a complex but not unexpected picture for the cantonal territory.
### Migration dynamics and balances Going into the detail of the numbers published by the Cantonal Office of Statistics, the overall migration balance for young people is positive. In other words, more 25 and 35-year-olds arrive than leave the cantonal territory. However, analyzing the direction of the flows, a critical issue emerges in movements within the Confederation. Between 2015 and 2024, the intercantonal balance proved negative, recording an average loss of 495 people per year heading towards other Swiss cantons. A significant part of this internal mobility has the city of Zurich as its final destination, attractive for professional and educational opportunities.
### The role of new arrivals Those who leave often find a new dimension north of the Alps, while those replacing the departing residents are mainly citizens coming from abroad, particularly from Italy. Statistical analysis confirms that the vast majority of those arriving in Ticino from across the borders come from the neighboring country, widely exceeding the departures recorded in the same period. This phenomenon compensates for the youth demographic loss, fitting into a broader context of cross-border and international labor mobility that has historically characterized the canton's economy and local labor market. The demographic dynamics analysed by the Cantonal Statistical Office (USTAT) offer important insights for the economic and social future of Ticino, especially when compared with forecasts on population ageing. Historically considered a Canton with a strong elderly component, Ticino faces structural challenges related to workforce management and territorial competitiveness. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO/SBB) predicts that, with the progressive retirement of baby boomers, competition to attract young workers between Switzerland and the European Union will intensify pressure on local markets.

This means that in the future even the territories of origin of migratory flows could be activated to retain the young local generations, potentially reducing the availability of a skilled workforce ready to move or work in the Confederation. item.title: Seasonal in Tourism: Featured Accommodation Expenses
item.description: A study by the University of Lausanne commissioned by the Federal Office of Housing analyzes the housing difficulties of seasonal workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - University of Lausanne study on seasonal workers - Commissioned by the Federal Housing Office - 95 interviews conducted in 4 tourist destinations - Housing expenses indicated as the main difficulty
## Key facts - What: Analysis of the housing situation of seasonal workers - When: September 11, 2026 - Where: Adelboden, Leysin, Saas-Fee and Villars-sur-Ollon - Who: University of Lausanne and Federal Housing Office - Amount: 95 total interviews, of which 84 with seasonal workers - Context: Co-financed by the Cantons of Bern, Vaud and Valais
The Swiss tourism sector cannot do without seasonal workers, but their presence is closely linked to the availability of adequate living spaces. A recent study conducted by the University of Lausanne, commissioned by the Federal Housing Office and co-financed by the Cantons of Bern, Vaud and Valais, has analyzed for the first time the housing situation from the perspective of seasonal workers. The report, entitled «Usages et besoins en logement des travailleurs saisonniers en stations de sports d'hiver», highlights the main problem encountered in this economic sector: housing expenses.
In Swiss alpine localities, rising rental prices heavily impact the budgets of temporary employees, whose cantonal minimum salaries average between 3,800 and 4,200 gross Swiss francs per month according to the collective employment agreements of the hotel and catering industry (L-GAV).
### Methodology and scope of the research Research is based on a total of 95 interviews, including 84 conducted directly with seasonal workers employed in the destinations of Adelboden, Leysin, Saas-Fee and Villars-sur-Ollon. Living spaces play a central role not only for the daily life of these people, but decisively influence the possibility of finding a job, the individual financial situation and the eventual decision to return to work in a specific tourist resort. The presence of an adequate housing supply therefore represents a crucial factor for tourist destinations, useful for attracting labor and retaining it over the long term, ensuring the operational continuity of local businesses.
> The housing crisis in tourist valleys directly threatens the competitiveness of our hotel and non-hotel system.
### Practical scenarios and financial impact In Saas-Fee and Adelboden, a standard studio apartment for the winter season can exceed 1,200 francs per month, absorbing up to thirty percent of the net salary of an unskilled seasonal worker. To make a comparison with urban centers like Zurich or Geneva, where cost per square meter is high but offset by higher average salaries, in tourist resorts the ratio between fixed rental costs and seasonal income of 4-5 months creates a structural savings deficit for foreign employees or inter-cantonal commuters. Companies that provide company housing at subsidized prices, often obtained from old annexes or converted hotel rooms, record staff retention rates forty-five percent higher than those who leave workers free to find a roof on the free alpine real estate market. Analyzing the housing needs that emerged from the interviews, industry operators and local authorities are facing well-defined priorities indicated by workers. The research highlights that finding affordable housing represents the absolute need. High housing costs relative to income drastically reduce the possibility of setting aside savings during the season. In Graubünden and Valais, where the average cost of a studio apartment often exceeds 1'200 Swiss francs per month, seasonal workers who earn a gross minimum salary of around 3'800 francs according to the Collective Employment Agreement for the hotel and catering industry find themselves allocating over 35% of their income solely to rent. In addition to the economic factor, seasonal workers express the need to find housing solutions close to their workplace and the essential services of the location. Short routes simplify everyday life and reduce costs related to mobility, a particularly relevant aspect if one considers the sometimes irregular working hours typical of winter tourism and the adverse weather conditions of the cold season.
### Qualitative aspects and contractual flexibility As for the furnishings and quality of the housing, the priorities are not linked to high demands for comfort, but rather to cleanliness, adequate sizes, complete equipment and the possibility of enjoying a minimum of privacy. This need proves crucial in shared accommodation, where different schedules and life rhythms can complicate daily coexistence between colleagues. The fourth priority identified by the study concerns the flexibility of lease contracts. Often the duration of rental agreements does not coincide with that of the seasonal employment contract, generating unjustified additional costs for workers. Interviewees hope for flexible lease start and end dates and the possibility of re-renting the same accommodation in subsequent seasons, thus stabilizing the presence of workers in the alpine valleys.
- Rent commensurate with the cantonal minimum wage - Maximum distance of fifteen minutes on foot from the ski lifts - Minimum equipment with independent kitchen and internet connection included
> The stabilization of the workforce necessarily passes through a farsighted housing policy for the tourist valleys.

The housing situation for seasonal workers in the Swiss tourism sector varies considerably depending on the location, highlighting marked disparities between the various Alpine centers of the Confederation. The ease of finding suitable accommodation depends on critical factors such as local availability and prices, the percentage of secondary residences in the area pursuant to the Federal Act on Second Homes (L2H) which entered into force in 2016, the accessibility of transport links, and the housing supply available in neighboring municipalities.
Analyzing regional data, in locations such as Zermatt (Canton of Valais) or St. Moritz (Canton of Graubünden), where the real estate market is under severe pressure, costs for a single room for seasonal workers can easily exceed 900-1200 Swiss francs per month, heavily impacting gross salaries which, according to the Collective Employment Agreements (CEA) for the hotel and catering industry (L-GAV), generally range between 3850 and 4400 francs per month for staff without specific qualifications. Conversely, in peripheral valleys of Ticino or in smaller resorts of the Bernese Oberland, average prices often range between 550 and 750 francs, while still facing issues related to the aging of properties.
Workshops organized in the four examined destinations and discussions at the national level have demonstrated that there is no single solution valid everywhere, but rather the need to develop approaches tailored to local specificities.
### Operational measures for employers and Municipalities - Advance planning of bed requirements at least 6 months before the season - Conversion of commercial properties or disused hotels into employee residences - Establishment of long-term agreements with local owners to freeze rental fees - Sharing of housing resources among multiple companies in the same tourist destination
Employers and Municipalities are called upon to act in close collaboration with the Cantons, tourist organizations, and other local economic actors to develop concrete responses. The report by the University of Lausanne offers a practical working basis with various intervention possibilities, including tax reliefs for companies investing in the construction of staff housing and municipal building incentives that derogate from normal utilization rates.

The financial situation of Swiss hospitals recorded a slight improvement over the course of last year. Despite this positive sign, the overall context remains particularly tense for the Swiss healthcare sector. According to data released by the hospital umbrella association H+, over 80% of acute care facilities fail to reach the margin necessary to guarantee fully sustainable operations over time. The analysis conducted by the SpitalBenchmark association, which examined over 90% of the hospitals operating in Swiss territory, provides a detailed picture of this transitional phase.
### The trend of operating margins
Looking at the economic data collected by the analysis in detail, the average EBITDA margin of healthcare facilities, calculated by subtracting operating costs from revenues, showed an increase, rising from 4% to 5.6% during 2025. Nonetheless, this percentage level still remains markedly below the 10% threshold deemed essential by experts to ensure solid long-term management. The director of H+, Anne-Geneviève Bütikofer, highlighted how four out of five hospitals are still not generating the essential financial resources needed to make the necessary investments in qualified personnel, new technologies, and adequate infrastructure. Consequently, the Swiss healthcare sector is still a considerable distance away from a genuine structural turnaround. The Swiss hospital sector has reiterated its willingness to decisively strengthen outpatient care, a step considered strategic for effectively containing the overall costs of the national health system. However, healthcare facilities warn that such a radical transformation cannot take place without adequate financial resources and generally favorable framework conditions. The transition towards more modern and sustainable care models indeed requires massive initial investments which, in light of current margins, are difficult for the vast majority of Swiss hospitals to sustain.
### Criticisms of cost growth limitation
Within this complex scenario, the H+ association expressed a markedly critical evaluation of the decisions adopted by the Federal Council. Specifically, it challenges the measure that sets a maximum growth limit of 4% for outpatient costs. According to the estimates and concerns expressed by the hospital sector, a restriction of this magnitude realistically risks halting the transition towards outpatient care. Such a regulatory brake would inevitably end up calling into question the possibility of refinancing future investments, further hindering the path towards a modern and efficient Swiss healthcare system capable of responding to the demographic and economic challenges of the coming years without compromising the quality of services provided to patients residing in the various cantons.

Economiesuisse has a new leader: after two three-year terms, Christoph Mäder today handed over the presidency to his successor Silvan Wildhaber. item.description: The ASIB requires an increase of 2.5% in the wage bill and 2000 francs more for incomes up to 120,000francs for the 2026/2027 negotiations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - SBEA demands a 2.5% increase in the total salary mass in the banking sector. - An increase of at least 2,000 francs requested for salaries up to 120,000 francs. - Objective: protect purchasing power and share corporate profits. - Transparency required regarding the criteria for distributing salary increases.
## Key facts - **What**: Request for salary adjustments in the Swiss banking sector. - When: Ahead of the 2026/2027 salary negotiations. - Where: Credit institutions operating in Switzerland. - Who: Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBEA). - Amount: Increase of 2,000 francs per year for incomes up to 120,000 francs.
The Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBEA) has formalized its demands for the upcoming salary negotiations, aiming for a 2.5% increase in the total payroll. The claim, decided by the executive committee following discussions with staff representatives, aims to ensure that employees directly participate in the excellent economic results achieved by credit institutions. In addition to the overall percentage, the union specified a minimum threshold of 2,000 additional francs per year for all employees with an annual salary of up to 120,000 francs, calculated on a full-time basis. The SBEA clarified that this request is consistent with the adjustment of minimum wages provided for by the sector's collective labor agreement, which will rise by 2,000 francs starting from January 1, 2027.
### Transparency and distribution criteria A fundamental pillar of the SBEA strategy concerns the request for transparency in corporate decision-making processes. The union demands that banks clearly communicate the criteria used for the distribution of increases, allowing employees and staff representatives to understand the logic behind individual salary variations. The association also suggests that institutions review their salary bands, increasing them where necessary. The recommendation addressed to individual companies is to advance requests of this magnitude while taking into account the specific economic situation and the peculiarities of each individual firm. The ultimate goal remains to ensure that record profits, consistently recorded by various types of banks, from regional ones to large banks like UBS, translate into tangible benefits for the entire workforce that contributes to the institution's operational success. The economic justification put forward by ASIB to support its claims is based on three main pillars that directly affect the daily lives of workers. The first critical point is the maintenance of purchasing power. Despite inflation, the association highlights how the constant increase in health insurance premiums represents a burden not included in the official cost-of-living index, significantly eroding the disposable income of families. Forecasts for 2026 suggest inflation slightly higher than the previous year, with uncertainties linked to the geopolitical situation and the cost of oil that could further influence consumer prices. For those wishing to delve into the impact of fixed costs on the family budget, the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living) remains an essential parameter to monitor.
### The recovery of salary arrears The second point concerns the lack of salary adjustments accumulated during the years 2022 and 2023. During this period, characterized by high inflation, most banks did not provide full compensation for the rise in the cost of living. ASIB points out that, in many cases, employees have not seen pay raises for years, and even in the most recent two-year periods, adjustments have been rare and partial. This delay must, according to the association, be bridged to realign wages with the actual cost of living. Productivity represents the third pillar: the introduction of new digital technologies and artificial intelligence has allowed banks to optimize processes. At the same time, staff reductions in numerous institutions have increased the workload for those who remained. ASIB argues that if fewer employees provide the same or higher performance, productivity gains should be fairly redistributed. Workers, therefore, are not only asking for an adjustment to prices, but for recognition of the added value created through the operational efficiency and technological innovation that characterize the Swiss financial sector today.

For employees in the banking sector wishing to evaluate their contractual position, it is essential to conduct a thorough review of their remuneration. Although ASIB requests are made at a sector level, negotiations often take place at the individual company level. It is advisable to consult your bank's staff representatives to understand the scope for maneuver and whether the institution has already initiated a review of salary bands in response to union guidelines. The transparency requested by the ASIB should be viewed as a protective tool: every employee has the right to request clarification on performance evaluation criteria and the parameters that determine salary increases. In a time of technological transformation, where digitalization is redefining professional roles, knowledge of compensation dynamics becomes a strength in managing one's career.
### Tools for financial planning Beyond direct negotiation, it is appropriate to monitor how salary variations influence long-term pension planning. An increase in gross remuneration has positive repercussions on both the contributions paid into the second pillar and the ability to contribute to the third pillar. For those working in Switzerland, it is possible to use digital tools to calculate the net impact of any salary increases, considering tax deductions and mandatory social contributions. Awareness of one's contribution status, including AHV/BVG payments, is essential to optimize one's position for retirement. Remember that financial planning is a dynamic process that requires periodic reviews, especially in the presence of significant changes in the remuneration structure or corporate welfare policies, which often accompany year-end salary negotiations.
